answer: Seeded task uniqueness. Each identity must solve a fresh puzzle whose seed is drawn from a public randomness beacon, then submit a short solution thread that is checked against all prior solutions; duplicates are rejected. The puzzle mixes in a ferrous token encoding so solutions can't be precomputed offline. Because every answer must be unrepeatable, an attacker creating N identities pays N full solve costs plus wasted work on collisions, making mass duplication linearly expensive rather than cheap. A comet-seeded round closes each epoch.
